correctness.rationale: For every active curvature set, surjectivity of the second-difference map constructs a strictly complementary projection cell; the global piecewise-linear Euclidean projector consequently has maximum-norm Lipschitz constant equal to the maximum absolute row sum of its face matrices. Eight exact five-point matrices give unique face {1,3} and center-row value 11/7. The listed finite input pair satisfies primal feasibility and positive dual KKT multipliers. Padding a face matrix by identity proves monotonicity, and an explicitly inverted tridiagonal Gram matrix with geometrically dominated Green-kernel rows gives liminf ≥1+1/√2. The packaged standalone checker passed 420 exact rational checks, including face coverage, extremizers, embeddings and finite continuants; the infinite limit is separately proved analytically.

originality.rationale: Searches of semantically equivalent descriptions, broader first-difference projection settings, finite exact constants, and published shape-restricted regression literature returned no statement implying both the exact five-observation 11/7 transition and the alternating-curvature asymptotic lower bound. value.rationale: With five equally spaced sites, two nonadjacent zero-curvature faces first coexist. They yield a strict increase from the four-point sharp maximum 7/5 to 11/7 and a unique central output sensitivity hotspot. This is a natural, structurally motivated boundary for robustness of Euclidean convex least-squares regression. The alternating-curvature family supplies a substantive persistent lower bound for growing sample sizes rather than a purely low-dimensional numerical curiosity.
